prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1216; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment grew to many times the usual amount for this injury, with near-daily visits and new body areas added weeks after the crash.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured reported being rear-ended at a stop. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Spoke with the driver named on the policy, who confirmed the vehicle and coverage details. The driver's account of the collision matches the report received at intake.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report and statements from two independent witnesses. Both describe the other vehicle stopping abruptly and both confirm the claimant was seated in the vehicle at the time.

Entry 4: Reviewed the photographs from the scene and the other driver's statement. Both are consistent with the described impact, and the other driver confirms the accident happened as reported.

Entry 5: Inspected the vehicle. The damage is mostly in line with the described impact, and a few old scratches near the bumper may predate this crash and have been noted separately.

Entry 6: Received the claimant's initial injury report through counsel, describing a back strain. The reported injury is plausible for a collision of this type, and no prior injury to the same body area is known to us.

Entry 7: Took a recorded statement from the claimant through counsel. The account of the collision was the same as the one given at intake and in the earlier call with the claimant's office.

Entry 8: Reviewed the medical records as they came in. Treatment has increased to many times the usual amount for this injury, with near-daily visits and new body areas added several weeks after the crash.

Entry 9: Requested further records and an independent medical review to address the rise in treatment frequency and the new body areas. The review is pending and will be weighed against the earlier findings.

Entry 10: Checked the policy history. Nothing in the file suggests the damage occurred before the coverage began, and the coverage was in force at the time of loss.

Entry 11: Claim remains open pending the independent medical review and the attorney's response to the treatment questions. Reserves reviewed and will be updated once the review is received.
